name: Lip microneedling
lead: Lip microneedling applies the collagen induction technique, repeated puncturing of the skin with tiny sterile needles, to the lip area, with proponents aiming at finer lines and modest volume. General microneedling is used for scarring and acne, and research on it is described as ongoing.[1]
No studies specific to the lips were found for this entry, and sources are limited, so this article is short.

paras: Microneedling, also called collagen induction therapy or dermarolling, punctures the skin repeatedly with fine needles. It is used for scars and acne, and combinations with platelet-rich plasma have unproven efficacy pending studies.[1]

Infection is the main concern. In April 2024 the CDC reported HIV diagnoses in three women who had received platelet-rich-plasma microneedling facials at one unregulated spa, prompting warnings about non-medical settings.[1]
No studies found. Existing microneedling studies concern scarring and hair loss rather than lips.[1]

card.summary: Needling aimed at lip lines and volume; established for scars elsewhere but unstudied on lips.
card.note: Infection risk if done in non-medical settings.

quick.overview:
Lip microneedling uses fine needles on the lips to try to smooth lines and add a little fullness.

No lip-specific studies were found.
quick.mechanism: Tiny punctures are thought to trigger skin repair and collagen production.
quick.risks: Infection is the key concern, particularly with unregulated providers; a 2024 CDC report linked HIV cases to a spa microneedling facial.
